# Force Dark Mode - ThemeSwitcher

> Free, open-source (MIT) Chrome extension, Manifest V3, that applies dark themes to websites, PDFs and local documents. It processes pages and documents on the device; the only data that can leave it is an optional usage report (versions 2.0.0 and 2.1.0, opt-in) or a broken-site report the user starts and confirms (version 2.1.0 and later).

## Facts
- Name: Force Dark Mode - ThemeSwitcher
- Current version: 2.0.0 (12 October 2026)
- Platform: Google Chrome, Manifest V3
- License: MIT
- Users: 1,700+ weekly users and 3,900+ in total (Chrome Web Store developer dashboard, 21 October 2026)
- Website: https://darkmode.pshah.fun/
- Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/force-dark-mode/kmhhphbakbhohiohagkhhgdgfbplkfke
- Source code: https://github.com/pshah-lab/force-dark-mode-extension
- Maker: PshahLab, founded by Pratham Shah (https://pshah.fun)

## What it does
- Three theme engines: Auto (samples page luminance and picks an approach), CSS Override (recolors backgrounds and text by contrast) and Invert (inverts the page while keeping images and video as they are). An OLED preset uses pure black.
- Detects sites that already have a native dark theme and leaves them alone, to avoid double inversion.
- Injects styles at `document_start`, so pages don't flash white before the theme applies.
- Built-in offline document viewer: PDF (via a bundled PDF.js), Markdown, plain text, RTF, and since 1.7.0 read-only DOCX and PPTX, and since 2.0.0 read-only XLSX and CSV spreadsheets. Files are never uploaded.
- Since 2.0.0: eight built-in color themes, site packs for 20 popular sites (with fixes for 3, such as hindustantimes.com, npr.org and theguardian.com), a theme editor with a contrast check, theme import and export, and per-site custom CSS that is validated and cannot introduce a URL. Custom CSS can never cause a network request.
- Per-site settings, custom colors, brightness, contrast and sepia sliders, and scheduling by time range or the system dark-mode setting.
- Keyboard shortcuts: Alt+Shift+D toggles dark mode; Alt+Shift+O and Alt+Shift+V open the document viewer.

## Privacy
- Version 2.0.0: anonymous usage statistics are off by default and sent only after opt-in (random install ID, UTC day, version, Chrome version, OS family, language, and yes/no flags for engine, built-in theme and features; never sites, URLs or content); users can delete the data from Options > Usage stats, and only combined totals (groups under 10 installs hidden) are published at https://darkmode.pshah.fun/stats.html. Version 2.1.0 and later: the usage report is off by default and sent only after the user turns it on (random install ID, UTC day, version, yes/no flags for the engines used and a count of sites dark mode was applied on; never sites, URLs or content), and turning it off deletes the data stored for the ID; a broken-site report is sent only when the user presses Report this site as broken and confirms (four fields: site domain, engine, theme label, extension version; no ID); our server function does not store IP addresses and reports are purged after 13 months. Automated tests confine all network code to one file.
- Settings are stored in `chrome.storage`; users can export them as JSON or erase them in one click.
- This website counts visits with one cookie-free request per browser to pshah.fun. The extension sends data only if you opt in (the usage report, versions 2.0.0 and 2.1.0) or confirm a broken-site report (2.1.0 and later). Details: https://darkmode.pshah.fun/privacy.html

## Limitations
- Pages drawn on a canvas (for example some online document editors) can't be recolored with CSS.
- The Invert engine can double-invert some icons.
